messages:
ismael: Heads-up — monitoring flagged a slow-but-consistent rise in row-remap events on cluster8 (pool-D). Noticed across 4 different cards over the last 48h. https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cluster8
alertbot: [ALERT] ECC remap rate above baseline on rack8-gn05 (gpu3). 15 remaps in 6h. Pager: @sre-oncall
sre-oncall: On it. Can someone paste latest dmesg / nvidia output? Want to check Xid pattern.
jon: grabbing logs now, running quick `nvidia-smi -q` then `dmesg | grep -i nv` — will paste.
jon: ```
GPU 3:
  ECC Errors (Corrected): 412 -> 428 (+16)
  Volatile Remapped Pages: 3 -> 7
NVRM: Xid (13) 62: GPU exception, PC 0x7ff...
NVRM: remap event flagged for GPU 3
```
tara: that's the same Xid we saw in pool2 last month before vendor replacement. Card serial SZ-89-XXXX. Can we soft-drain this node? Also check adjacent GPUs on same board.
kai: ran address-scan job, found increasing remap counts on gpu2/gpu3/gpu5 across rack8-gn*. Pattern looks localized to rack8 series, not cluster-wide — could be a batch or PCB issue.
ismael: created vendor ticket VEND-2026-432 with logs + nvdiag bundle. Linking in ticket.
jon: temporary mitigation: setting soft_drain=true on rack8-gn05 and evacuating high-priority jobs from GPU3. Will keep it for low-priority/backfill until we have replacement.
sre-oncall: soft drain applied and kubesched evict started. :thumbsup: Will monitor eviction progress.
infra: before full replace, run overnight ECC stress + memtest on the 4 suspect cards. If remap counters continue to climb during stress, escalate to RMA.
kai: also proposing a monitoring rule change: add slow-alert if remap_rate > 3/hr sustained for 24h to catch gradual degradations vs spikes. I'll open PR in monitoring repo and link.
ismael: heads-up on capacity: pool-D losing ~12% capacity during drain — autoscaler should kick in but flagging potential latency increase for some jobs.
sre-oncall: opening maintenance window Sat 03:00-05:00 UTC for vendor swap if memtest fails. Adding oncall rotation for handover. 
jon: attaching CSV of per-card page-retire counters to vendor ticket (VEND-2026-432) — shows steady hourly increases on suspect cards vs baseline cards which are flat.
tara: good work. If we see Xid change to anything other than 62 (e.g., new codes 31/48), call vendor on the war room channel immediately.
infra: tagging weekend coverage: @sre-weekend — please monitor the slow-alert until we confirm memtest results.
sre-weekend: acknowledged, will watch graphs overnight and post any upticks.
sre-oncall: summary: soft-drain applied, memtests scheduled, vendor ticket open (VEND-2026-432), maintenance window booked. Keep updates here and in the ticket. Closing Slack thread for active action — will reopen if Xid pattern changes or remap rate accelerates. :calendar:
